_meta.title: GH #368 — ui-nav-rail collapse="menu" adopts the fleet Overlay controller (top-layer, anchored, bordered card)
_meta.v2_1_diff: Delta pass on v2 (doc-checker, 2026-07-30) — three mechanical fixes, no structural change (node/action/edge counts unchanged at 25/34/24). N1 (MAJOR): five negated greps in n2/n5/n18 used literal `...` ellipsis paths; `grep -q pattern <missing path>` exits 2 and `!` inverts that to SUCCESS (verified empirically in this worktree), so those checks — INCLUDING the two enforcing Kim's <details> ruling — would have greened while examining nothing. Every path is now spelled in full AND guarded `test -f <path> && ! grep -q …`; the guard is applied to n9/n10b/n11/n15/n19 too, since a RENAME defeats a full path just as a typo does. An audit script now confirms zero unguarded negated greps and zero ellipsis paths remain. N2: `open_fork_panel_width` renamed `ruling_panel_width` (it advertised an open fork over settled FIRM content) and its trigger-width residual lifted into a top-level `deferred` list so a fresh context scanning for blockers cannot misread it. N3: the container-introspection precondition was PROBED rather than assumed — see _meta.container_introspection_finding — and n4a now carries the resolution algorithm as a stated implementation fact. Also folded: n9 gains `summary` + `zero-JS` greps and n19 gains a `disclosure` grep (the sites with no 'details' substring, previously unforced); the ARIA note now cites menu.ts:48-51, which states the host-vs-parts rule verbatim.
_meta.v2_diff_original: (v2, superseded by v2.1 above — kept for reconstructability)
_meta.v2_diff: Revision after the FIX-FIRST doc-checker pass. Both headline conclusions upheld (no-ADR; the full-bleed reframing). Folded in: Kim's two rulings (<details> is retired for a plain button + overlay panel; ui-nav-rail earns a full site doc page + a visual test), the four blockers F1-F4, and F5-F14. Nodes 16 -> 25. Both negative controls were INERT and are replaced with biting ones (F1). The threshold bridge had no mechanism and is now split into a mechanism leaf + an outcome leaf (F2). collapse-container="ancestor" is now in scope (F3). The a11y regression <details> was hiding has its own leaf (F4).
_meta.verdict: BUG FIX inside the existing contract — NO ADR.
why_no_adr: The fleet already owns exactly one mechanism for 'a floating panel anchored to a trigger': the Overlay controller (traits/overlay.ts) + platform-owned dismissal — agent-ui-component-patterns' own row, ADR-0043 + ADR-0045. Adopting a row that already exists is not a fork.

SPEC-R5 AC2 ALREADY requires the panel to open 'overlaying the page (not reflowing it)' and be 'keyboard-dismissable (Escape or outside-click)'. position:absolute under-satisfies an accepted AC; satisfying it fully is a repair, not a new contract.

ADR-0130 cl.6 already routes the sibling icon-popover arm through the same shipped overlay primitives, citing ADR-0043/0045. The menu arm joining them REDUCES the family's overlay mechanisms from two to one.

ADR-0130 contains NO clause requiring position:absolute or a zero-JS disclosure. LLD-C4's '<details> ported from _page.css' is a PORTING-FIDELITY note about provenance, not a ruled constraint — and the component already deliberately broke zero-JS by adding its own Escape/outside-click listeners (nav-rail.ts #wireDisclosure, self-documented as 'a deliberate upgrade the componentization earns').
The overlay CONTRACT is unchanged: same trait, same popover=auto light-dismiss, same ADR-0101 announce contract, same focus round-trip. Only this one arm's WIRING changes.
kim_rulings_2026_07_30: RULING 1 — <details> GOES. The menu arm becomes a plain <button data-part="trigger"> + a [data-part="list"] overlay panel, the ui-popover shape. This de-hedges n2/n9/n15 (no 'if the wrapper goes' conditionals survive) and forces the chevron/marker CSS retirement (n18) plus the SPEC/LLD/descriptor records leaves (n9, n10b, n19, n11).

RULING 2 — ui-nav-rail earns a full site doc page matching its four app-tier siblings (super-shell.html, chat-shell.html, master-detail.html, settings.html) — page + site-manifest row + regenerated sitemap (n20, n21) — AND a nav-rail.visual.browser.test.ts pinning the open menu card (n22).
_meta.menu_vs_icon_popover_divergence: The two arms diverge in CONTENT MODEL, never in overlay mechanism. icon-popover flattens one group's items into a composed ui-menu (menuitem semantics). collapse="menu" collapses the WHOLE grouped rail — context-label headings (SPEC-R6) + name|tag two-column rows (ADR-0130 cl.7) — which ui-menu's menuitem content model cannot carry without losing both. So the menu arm calls overlay() DIRECTLY on its own panel, the ui-popover precedent (a generic disclosure overlay over arbitrary content), rather than composing ui-menu. Same trait, different content model.
_meta.anchor_positioning_finding: Do NOT bet the fix on CSS anchor positioning. Measured in this repo's own gate: both engines report CSS.supports true for anchor-name / position-anchor / position-area / position-try-fallbacks — but Playwright's bundled WebKit is NOT Safari-release, so a green gate would NOT prove real-world support. traits/overlay.ts already ruled this: 'CSS anchor-positioning is a PROGRESSIVE ENHANCEMENT ... NOT a v1 dual-path requirement; the JS controller is the reliable path.' The JS measure-and-place controller (computePosition: flip + shift) needs no support bet and is already cross-engine-proven by menu/select/tooltip/popover.
_meta.per_side_border_finding: Measured, both engines, panel open: borderTop/Right/Bottom/Left all compute to 1px in the correct outline color. The border is NOT missing — nav-rail.css:247's shorthand applies on all four sides. The real defect is that inset-inline:0 (nav-rail.css:243) makes the panel FULL-BLEED (measured listW=300 == railW=300, listLeft=0 == railLeft=0), so its side borders sit exactly on the rail's own edges and read as the shell's edge rather than the menu's own card outline. Kim's 'border on all sides' is the perceptual report of a full-bleed band. Both halves of the report share ONE root cause, and one mechanism change fixes both — do NOT 'add' borders.
_meta.clipping_reproduced: Measured, both engines: rail inside a single overflow:hidden ancestor 44px tall, panel opened — listTop=28 listBottom=122 vs clipperBottom=44, fullyInsideClipper=false, overflowBy=78px. 78 of the panel's 94px are clipped: ~83% of the menu invisible. The GH #260 class, reproduced cross-engine.
_meta.negative_control_law: Both NCs in v1 were INERT (F1). Recorded so no build re-derives them: (a) restoring `position: absolute` does NOT defeat the clipping probe — a [popover] promoted by showPopover() paints in the top layer regardless of its `position` value, so top-layer MEMBERSHIP is the biting variable; the NC must remove the popover attribute / skip showPopover(). `list.matches(':popover-open')` can never bite in that NC because it is exactly what the NC removes. (b) restoring the stylesheet `inset-inline: 0` does NOT defeat the card-geometry probe — overlay.ts:189-194 writes INLINE position/top/left/bottom/right/margin, which beat any stylesheet inset; the biting variable is the width clamp, so the NC must remove min/max-inline-size (overlay.ts never writes width).

ruling_panel_width.status: SETTLED — FIRM, not an open fork. Reviewed and conceded by the doc-checker delta pass (2026-07-30).
ruling_panel_width.question: Is the open panel content-sized (ui-menu/ui-popover precedent) or stretched to at least its trigger's width (the select-dropdown idiom)?
ruling_panel_width.ruling: CONTENT-SIZED, with a min-inline-size floor and a max-inline-size ceiling — the ui-menu/ui-popover precedent.
ruling_panel_width.why: A raw `list.width < rail.width` assertion over-constrains and is content-accidental, so the review's F6 was right to challenge it. But its proposed replacement — an ANCHOR-WIDTH clamp — cannot be the target here: the narrow trigger is a full-width flex box (nav-rail.css:190-219), so 'floor >= trigger width' is identically the full-bleed band that IS the defect Kim reported; the idiom inverts on this control. Content-sized is therefore the only option that satisfies the report. n6's predicate is where this is decided: a CONTROLLED fixture (deliberately short labels in a 300px rail) makes the assertion fixture-determined rather than content-accidental, and the biting NC is the clamp removal, not a width comparison. The delta review verified the trigger geometry at source and withdrew F6.

_meta.aria_law_note: n17 puts aria-expanded/aria-controls on a control-CREATED part (the button trigger), not on the host. This is settled fleet law, stated in as many words at menu.ts:48-51 — 'a created part, not the host — the FACE rule "internals.role, never host attributes" applies to the HOST element; direct parts use setAttribute' — and realized in ui-popover (popover.ts:130 for aria-expanded in an effect off `open`, popover.ts:182 for aria-controls at part creation). Recorded with the citation so the objection is foreclosed rather than re-litigated.
_meta.blast_radius: SMALLER than the report assumes, and the risk is on the DEFAULT path instead. No shipped consumer rides collapse="menu": site/pages/_page.ts:618 sets collapse="none" (GH #170/ADR-0155 moved the site's narrow story to ui-super-shell) and settings.ts:164 sets collapse="drill-in". BUT 'menu' is the enum's index-0 DEFAULT (nav-rail.ts:64), so every <ui-nav-rail> that omits collapse gets the broken arm — the defect is on the default, which is why it still matters. Kim's ruling 2 also closes the surface gap: ui-nav-rail currently has NO site doc page, NO gallery specimen and NO sitemap row, so nothing demonstrates or visually guards the arm being repaired.
_meta.shell_spec_check: Neither shell-archetypes-m5 clause constrains this. SPEC-R12 is a `display`-override/scope-proximity law (relevant only as a caution if a consumer ever overrides the panel's scoped display — it must tag-qualify). SPEC-R14/AC21's mid-window overlay is the SHELL's own pane-sized float, deliberately 'absolute over the canvas, inset within the middle row' so AC20's zero-overflow sweep holds — a different concept from a trigger-anchored flyout. SPEC-R14a's 'the toggle stays visible, aria-truthful' is however RULED LAW for the sibling shell and is the precedent n17 (F4) answers to. Risk to verify at build: AC20's zero-overflow sweep must stay green now that a nav-rail panel opened inside the shell can escape to the top layer.
_meta.first_in_package: packages/agent-ui/app has NO *.visual.browser.test.ts today (visual coverage exists only in components/{calendar,text} and site/pages). n22 is therefore the FIRST visual baseline in @agent-ui/app; its baselines land in packages/agent-ui/app/src/controls/nav-rail/__baselines__/nav-rail.visual.browser.test.ts/ (tracked — __screenshots__/ is gitignored failure output, .gitignore:44, not baselines).
_meta.container_introspection_finding: N3, PROBED not assumed (both engines, throwaway probe run 2026-07-30 then deleted): `getComputedStyle(el).containerName` and `.containerType` are readable and IDENTICAL in Chromium and WebKit — a container returns its own name ('ui-nav-rail-collapse') and type ('inline-size'), a non-container returns the clean sentinels 'none' and 'normal'; `getPropertyValue('container-name')` works equivalently and `'containerName' in decl` is true. So n4a IS buildable, and the downstream stall risk (n4b/n4c/n8/n16) is closed. STATED IMPLEMENTATION FACT for n4a's resolution algorithm: from the rail, walk self-then-ancestors and take the FIRST element whose computed `containerType !== 'normal'` AND whose computed `containerName` includes 'ui-nav-rail-collapse'; that element is the box the `@container ui-nav-rail-collapse` query resolves against, and it is the box the ResizeObserver must watch. Under collapse-container='self' the walk terminates on the rail itself; under 'ancestor' the rail's own containerType is 'normal' (nav-rail.css:84-86) so the walk continues upward — which is exactly why n4c discriminates a wrong-box observer.
deferred: Whether the narrow TRIGGER should also stop spanning the full rail width (nav-rail.css:190-219) is a separate visual decision this wave does NOT settle. The n22 visual baseline pins whatever it renders, so any later change is a deliberate baseline update rather than a silent drift. Not a blocker on this wave.
unanticipated: STALE DOC (live docs page): site/pages/super-shell.ts:232-235 still teaches 'the docs site's own nav pane uses this so ui-nav-rail's collapse="menu" dropdown takes over instead of the shell's hide/overlay arm (see it live in this very page's nav rail, narrow)'. False since GH #170/ADR-0155 — _page.ts sets collapse="none". Node n11.

FREE RIDER: nav-rail-family.spec.md's header calls ADR-0130 '(proposed — the six ratifying clauses this SPEC realizes)'. ADR-0130 is accepted (2026-07-12, ratified by Kim) with SEVEN clauses. Both wrong; repaired by n10b while that header is already open.

Kim's screenshot cannot be sourced to any current repo surface (the only in-repo rail runs collapse="none"). Worth confirming which surface it came from before the build freezes its reproduction case.

The a11y regression is silent and easy to ship: <summary> inside <details> got aria-expanded FREE from the UA, and overlay() manages ZERO ARIA (verified: no aria writes anywhere in traits/overlay.ts). Retiring <details> without n17 would trade a clipping bug for an accessibility bug.

nodes.label: mechanism: the CSS->JS threshold bridge — width observation that arms/disarms the overlay
nodes.accept: `npm run check` and `npm test` exit 0, and nav-rail.ts implements the STATED resolution algorithm (see _meta.container_introspection_finding, probed in both engines — the readability precondition is DISCHARGED, not assumed): from the rail, walk self-then-ancestors and take the FIRST element whose computed `containerType !== 'normal'` AND whose computed `containerName` includes 'ui-nav-rail-collapse'; observe THAT box with a ResizeObserver. The threshold comes from its single named source — `test -f packages/agent-ui/app/src/controls/nav-rail/nav-rail.ts && grep -q 'SHELL_NARROW_BREAKPOINT_REM' packages/agent-ui/app/src/controls/nav-rail/nav-rail.ts` succeeds and no bare `40` literal is introduced (shell-breakpoint.ts:13 is the literal's one owner; shell-breakpoint.test.ts is the drift gate). nodes.label: mechanism: the arming outcome — wide is inline, narrow is an overlay
nodes.accept: BOTH-ENGINE: at a 900px wrapper `[data-part="list"]` is visible in flow, has NO `popover` attribute, `:popover-open` is false, computed `position` !== 'fixed', and the trigger computes `display: none`; at a 300px wrapper the trigger is visible and the list is not rendered until activated. Crossing the threshold live (resize the wrapper 900px -> 300px -> 900px) lands in the correct state each time with no stranded popover attribute.

nodes.label: mechanism: collapse-container="ancestor" keeps working in both bands (F3)
nodes.accept: BOTH-ENGINE, reusing the existing `mountRailInNamedAncestor` fixture (nav-rail.browser.test.ts:82): with `collapse-container="ancestor"` and a WIDE named ancestor around a narrow column, the rail renders its inline vertical list and arms NO overlay; with a NARROW named ancestor, the trigger is visible and activation opens the top-layer panel. Non-vacuous: an observer watching the rail's OWN box (`this`) instead of the resolved container box makes the wide-ancestor case FAIL. `npm test` also exits 0 including the descriptor gate at nav-rail.test.ts:594 which pins this prop.

nodes.label: mechanism: retire BOTH hand-rolled dismissal listeners (superseded by platform light-dismiss)

nodes.label: a11y: the trigger's aria-expanded + aria-controls move into host code (F4)
nodes.accept: BOTH-ENGINE: `[data-part="trigger"]`'s `aria-expanded` reads 'false' when closed and 'true' when open across EVERY path — pointer click, Enter, Space, Escape, outside-click, and a programmatic open/close — and `aria-controls` resolves to the panel's real id (`document.getElementById(trigger.getAttribute('aria-controls')) === list`). Non-vacuous: <summary> got aria-expanded FREE from the UA and overlay() writes zero ARIA, so omitting the host wiring makes every one of these assertions fail. The ui-popover precedent is the shape (popover.ts:130 in an effect off `open`; aria-controls once at part creation, popover.ts:182); SPEC-R14a's 'aria-truthful' is the sibling shell's ruled law.

nodes.label: geometry: the panel becomes a content-sized floating card (nav-rail.css)
nodes.accept: BOTH-ENGINE, with the panel open on a CONTROLLED fixture (deliberately short item labels in a 300px rail): all four of borderTopWidth/RightWidth/BottomWidth/LeftWidth compute to 1px in the `--ui-nav-rail-outline` color; computed `min-inline-size` and `max-inline-size` each parse as a resolved LENGTH matching /^[0-9.]+px$/ (asserting `!== 'none'` is vacuous — min-inline-size's initial computed value is `auto`, F5); and the panel is strictly narrower than the rail on that fixture (content-driven; `inset-inline: 0` gone). nodes.label: geometry: panel block-size cap + stays fully on-screen
nodes.accept: BOTH-ENGINE: a 40-item rail's open panel satisfies `rect.bottom <= window.innerHeight` AND `rect.top >= 0` (F7 — v1's `height <= innerHeight` permitted a panel that fits but sits off-screen) AND `list.scrollHeight > list.clientHeight` — a long rail's panel scrolls rather than escaping the viewport (the menu.css `--ui-menu-max-block-size` precedent, including its border-box +2px lesson).

nodes.label: geometry: wide-arm inline integrity — no overlay residue, no stranded popover attribute
nodes.accept: BOTH-ENGINE: after an open -> close -> resize-to-wide cycle, `list.style.position === ''`, `list.style.top === ''`, `list.style.left === ''`, `list.style.right === ''`, `list.style.margin === ''` AND `list.hasAttribute('popover') === false`; the list's rect top equals the rail's content-box top (inline, in flow). This leaf must record WHY it exists (F13): overlay() has NO reset path — it writes those six inline styles on every position() (overlay.ts:189-194), clears none of them in cleanup() (overlay.ts:334-350), and never un-sets the popover attribute it sets at :165.
